Objective: This study investigated POGs effects on AA and its mechanisms in regulating M2 macrophage polarization. Methods: LC-MS profiled the SD/Prunus mume (PM) combination, and network pharmacology predicted its main active components and key anti-AA mechanisms. Ovalbumin (OVA) plus IL-4 established AA models in mice and RAW264.7 cells. Lung protection was assessed by histopathology, lung indices, and type II immune inflammatory cytokine markers. Flow Cytometry, RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence, and Western blot examined key genes/proteins in the JAK2-STAT6-PPAR{gamma} axis. Results: LC-MS-based network pharmacology identified POG as the key SD/PM active ingredient alleviating AA. Pharmacodynamic evaluation showed POG effectively alleviated OVA-induced airway inflammation and pulmonary histopathological damage in AA mice. Mechanistically, POG inhibited M2 macrophage polarization by downregulating key JAK2-STAT6-PPAR{gamma} axis factors. Conclusion: POG ameliorates AA by reducing type II immune factor release through JAK2-STAT6-PPAR{gamma}-mediated inhibition of M2 macrophage polarization. This study clarifies POGs anti-AA mechanism and supports its clinical development.

items.title: From CSP7 to CSP5: Development of a soluble, truncated congener for the treatment of obstructive and restrictive lung diseases.
items.corresponding_institution: University of Texas Health Science Center at Tyler
items.abstract: Chronic obstructive and restrictive lung diseases (CLDs), represent a substantial worldwide health burden, with curative therapies remaining largely unavailable. Studies from our group and others have identified caveolin-1 (Cav1)-mediated signaling as a critical regulator of cellular processes implicated in the pathogenesis and progression of CLDs, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), silicosis and other progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PF) conditions. We have previously demonstrated that Cav1 scaffolding domain peptides (CSP and CSP7), attenuate lung injury and PF across multiple preclinical mouse models and exhibit protective and anti-fibrotic effects in COPD and IPF tissues ex vivo. The mechanism involves concurrent suppression of p53 and its downstream signaling in lung (airway and alveolar) epithelial cells by competitively counteracting excess Cav1, while restoring baseline p53 levels in (myo)fibroblasts persisting in fibrotic lungs, and alternatively polarized alveolar macrophages (AMs) by complementing Cav1 function. The safety and tolerability of inhaled micronized CSP7 dry powder (aka LTI-03), have been evaluated in mice, rats, dogs, followed by a Phase 1a clinical trial assessing safety and pharmacokinetics in healthy volunteers (NCT04233814) and a Phase 1b trial in patients with IPF (NCT05954988). LTI-03 has subsequently advanced to a multicenter Phase 2 clinical trial in patients with IPF (NCT06968845). However, the FDA highlighted findings of minimal bronchiolar mucus cell metaplasia and hyperplasia in the 26-week rat inhalation study, raisings concerns regarding the suitability of poorly soluble CSP7 for long-term administration in patients with CLDs, particularly for COPD, a disease already characterized by goblet cell metaplasia and hyperplasia, mucus hypersecretion, impaired mucociliary clearance, and small airway obstruction. To address these limitations, we identified CSP5, a five amino acid truncated derivative of CSP7. Notably, the amorphous CSP5 attenuated p53 activation and apoptosis in preclinical models of tobacco smoke (TS)-, bleomycin, and silica-induced lung injury, demonstrating its potential to protect against epithelial injury across diverse lung disease models. Additionally, CSP5 enhanced surfactant protein C expression, consistent with alveolar epithelial cell homeostasis and regeneration, while suppressing Mucin 5Ac expression and attenuating distal lung injury in mice chronically exposed to TS. Furthermore, CSP5 promoted resolution of established PF in mouse models of bleomycin- or silica-induced fibrosis. CSP7, encompassing the CSP5 sequence, attenuates autophagic dysregulation, endoplasmic reticulum stress, reactive oxygen species, mitochondrial membrane potential abnormalities, and mitochondrial superoxide production, and profibrotic polarization of AMs in mice with PF. Collectively, these findings position CSP5 as a formidable next-generation peptide with preserved bioactive motif of CSP7 while offering improved physicochemical and potential advantages in formulation flexibility. The dominant features of CSP5 support its further development for chronic inhaled or systemic administration in the treatment of obstructive or fibrotic lung diseases.

items.title: Docking and SPR identify candidate interactions between Apolipoprotein A-I and chemokine receptors
authors: van der Vorst, E. P. C.
items.last_author: van der Vorst, E. P. C.
items.abstract: Background: Apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1), the main protein component of high-density lipoprotein, suppresses chemokine-driven leukocyte migration. This effect is usually attributed to indirect mechanisms such as cholesterol efflux, changes in lipid rafts, and altered receptor expression. Whether ApoA1 interacts with chemokine receptors directly is not known. Methods: We combined in silico rigid-body docking of AlphaFold-predicted structures (GRAMM-X, with interface analysis by PDBePISA) and surface plasmon resonance (SPR). In SPR experiments, ApoA1 was immobilized on the sensor, and CCR1, CCR5, CX3CR1, CXCR2, and CXCR4 were incorporated into proteoliposomes and injected as analytes. Mock proteoliposomes lacking any receptor served as a negative control. Kinetics were fitted with a 1:1 Langmuir model. Results: Docking predicted favorable interfaces between ApoA1 and all five receptors. CCR1 had the most favorable docking interaction, and CCR5 had the largest predicted interface (3716.7 A;iG -62.8 kcal/mol). Mock proteoliposomes showed no detectable binding to ApoA1, whereas all five receptors bound to ApoA1 in the SPR experiments. The apparent equilibrium dissociation constants (KD) were 3.44x10^-8 M for CXCR4, 3.96x10^-8 M for CXCR2, 5.26x10^-8 M for CCR5, 4.35x10^-7 M for CCR1, and 1.23x10^-6 M for CX3CR1. Conclusions: ApoA1 appears to bind chemokine receptors directly, with the highest apparent affinities for CXCR4, CXCR2, and CCR5. These findings suggest a candidate mechanism, complementary to cholesterol efflux and receptor expression regulation, by which ApoA1 may influence chemokine signaling. However, whether binding alters receptor signaling, internalization, or cell migration remains to be determined.

items.title: Pathogenic role of cGAS-STING pathway in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
items.corresponding_institution: Smidt Heart Institute, Cedars-Sinai Medical Center
items.abstract: The cGAS-STING pathway is a critical component of the innate immune response to infection and cell stress. Chronic activation underlies human diseases such as lupus and inflammatory bowel disease, but cGAS-STING has not been implicated in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). Compared to healthy controls, macrophages from DMD patients have high levels of cytosolic DNA and low levels of the DNA exonuclease, TREX1, a scavenger of cytosolic DNA upstream of cGAS-STING. Likewise, cytosolic DNA is elevated in macrophages from dystrophin-deficient mdx mice. Such macrophages over-produce cGAMP and secrete it locally, activating STING in neighboring myoblasts and thereby suppressing myogenesis. TY1, a synthetic non-coding RNA drug that enhances TREX1, attenuates cGAS-STING and restores cellular and tissue homeostasis in mdx mice. When administered intravenously or orally, TY1 not only halted disease progression but actually reversed cardiac and skeletal muscle pathology. Thus, pathological activation of cGAS-STING by cytosolic DNA mediates disease progression in DMD. Our work identifies TREX1, cGAS and STING as novel therapeutic targets in muscular dystrophy.

items.title: Spatial coordination of filamentous enzymes establishes a redox-balancing metabolon
items.abstract: Nutrient scarcity in tumors prompts metabolic adaptations in cancer cells. Here, we identify that glutamine deprivation, a common feature of the tumor microenvironment, induces formation of a proline biosynthesis metabolon to selectively maintain intracellular proline levels. Mechanistically, filament-forming enzymes glutaminase (GLS) and pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthase (P5CS) co-assemble with the downstream reductases PYCR1 and PYCR2 into a physically associated enzyme complex within a spatially segregated mitochondrial subset. This assembly is dynamically regulated by the pathway intermediate glutamate and is membrane-anchored via ATP synthase. Disruption of enzyme spatial coordination compromises pathway activity, while the sustained proline biosynthesis is repurposed to support redox homeostasis under limited glutamine. We reveal nutrient-responsive filamentation and spatial coordination of mitochondrial enzymes as a mechanism of rapid metabolic adaptation to the fluctuating cellular environment.

items.title: Targeted siRNA screening coupled with unbiased proteomics identify potassium signaling as a critical regulator of pigmentation
items.abstract: Ion channels are emerging as critical regulators of cellular signaling, influencing diverse pathophysiological processes and offering promising opportunities for therapeutic intervention. However, the contribution of ionic homeostasis to human skin pigmentation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify potassium (K+) dynamics as a critical regulator of pigmentation and uncover K+ channel Kir7.1 as a molecular link between K+ and cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling. A targeted siRNA screen identified six previously unrecognized regulators of pigmentation, which we validated using mouse cell line systems, primary human melanocytes, and an in vivo zebrafish model. Unbiased proteomic analyses of two prominent screening hits, Rhot1 and VDAC3, led us to identify Kir7.1, a plasma membrane-localized K+ channel, as a key determinant of pigmentation. Integrating cellular, molecular, ultrastructural, and microscopy approaches, we demonstrate functional crosstalk between the hits and Kir7.1 channel activity. Mechanistically, Kir7.1 promotes the canonical cAMP-protein kinase A (PKA) pathway, establishing this channel as a molecular node that couples K+ dynamics to the classical melanogenic pathway. Notably, Kir7.1 is differentially expressed in skin pigmentary disorders such as vitiligo and melasma, highlighting its therapeutic potential. Taken together, our findings establish Kir7.1 as an important regulator of skin pigmentation and reveal an unanticipated connection between K+ homeostasis, mitochondrial Ca2+ handling toolkit, and cAMP-dependent melanogenesis. This work provides a foundation for exploring K+ signaling as a potential therapeutic avenue for human pigmentary disorders.

items.title: WormIE: an Integrated Explorer for multi-source Caenorhabditis elegans annotations and transcriptomic data interpretation
items.abstract: Interpreting gene lists and expression data from Caenorhabditis elegans experiments usually means writing scripts, searching scattered databases or uploading unpublished data to a remote server. WormIE (Worm Integrated Explorer, https://wormie.bio) is a free, open-source tool for analyzing user-provided data and exploring C. elegans annotations in one browser tab. Starting with gene lists from -omics experiments, genetic screens or other approaches, users can explore what genes have in common and how they interact, test over-representation or ranked-list enrichment in built-in or user-provided gene sets and compare lists by their genes or enriched categories. Of WormIE's nine collections, which include Gene Ontology and CeNGEN neuron types, two are curated sets found in no other worm resource: neuronal genes and synaptic genes. WormIE counts aligned reads from RNA sequencing and tests for differential expression with the same R package as conventional pipelines, then checks the genes for enrichment in those collections. Clicking any gene in a result page opens the gene page gathering seventeen domains from WormBase, the Alliance of Genome Resources and other sources, such as phenotypes, interactions and expression. Everything runs on the user's computer without uploading data and works offline. On simulated data, every analysis agreed with its R counterpart (correlation 0.9999), and in a reanalysis of a germline study of the co-regulator SIN-3, WormIE recovered 99% of the reported differentially expressed genes and all nine WormCat categories. Together, these results show that WormIE reliably links gene lists and expression data to community-curated knowledge without programming or a server.

items.title: Vecmatch: Balancing Covariates in Multiple Groups Using Vector Matching Algorithm and Generalized Propensity Scores
items.abstract: Covariate imbalance is a major source of bias in observational studies. This issue arises when confounding variables (e.g., age, sex) are distributed unevenly across compared groups, potentially influencing estimates of between-group differences in other dependent variables. Matching techniques based on propensity scores are widely used to address covariate imbalance and improve the accuracy of causal inferences. These methods work by calculating propensity scores based on imbalanced covariates and then matching observations with the closest propensity scores across compared groups. However, existing matching methods primarily focus on comparisons between at most two groups, and there is currently no widely implemented approach for matching across more than two treatment groups in popular programming languages. In this paper, we present an R implementation of the vector matching algorithm for matching across multiple treatment groups. The implementation includes the core algorithm itself along with several extensions aimed at improving usability and flexibility in applied research. These features include tools for visualizing covariate distributions, functions for estimating generalized propensity scores, and methods for defining rectangular regions of common support. Users can choose among different matching methods and adjust various parameters to improve covariate balance. To support this process, we provide an optimization workflow based on the random search algorithm that identifies parameter combinations yielding the best matching quality and highest percentage of matched samples. In addition, the package includes functions for assessing post-matching quality, offering a comprehensive and flexible framework for robust causal inference in complex observational settings. Keywords: covariate imbalance, bias reduction, vector matching, generalized propensity scores

items.title: Characterization of Inter-Alpha-Trypsin Inhibitor Heavy Chain 5 (ITIH5) Expression, a Prostate Basal Cell Marker.
items.corresponding_institution: The University of Alabama at Birmingham, USA
items.abstract: The prostate epithelium contains secretory luminal epithelial cells, basal epithelial cells and neuroendocrine cells. Luminal cells are secretory cells that produce prostatic secretions and basal cells are involved in regeneration and maintenance of epithelial tissue. The absence of a basal cell layer is a defining morphological feature of prostate adenocarcinoma. Immunohistochemical detection of basal cells using standard markers such as p63 and high molecular weight keratin (34{beta}E12) is routinely employed to differentiate invasive carcinoma from benign architecture mimics. Additional protein like TRIM29 and ETS2 are also known to stain prostatic basal cells. While recent advances in sequencing and proteomic technologies helped identify many luminal epithelial markers for prostate cancers, basal cells are less investigated. In the current study, we identified Inter-Alpha-Trypsin Inhibitor Heavy Chain 5 (ITIH5) as a gene expressed exclusively in the basal cells of prostate epithelium. ITIH5 is a hyaluronan-stabilizing extracellular matrix protein that has been shown to be downregulated by promoter DNA hypermethylation in various cancers. Gene expression analysis using published dataset suggested ITIH5 is expressed in prostate basal cells compared to luminal cells. To characterize the potential diagnostic utility of ITIH5 in prostatic tissues, we evaluated its immunohistochemical expression profile across benign and malignant prostatic glands. Our immunohistochemistry analysis confirmed that ITIH5 protein is mainly in the cytoplasmic compartment of basal cells lining benign prostatic acini while prostate luminal cells showed no signal for ITIH5. Importantly, the cytoplasmic staining of ITIH5 reflected the nuclear staining of p63 in terms of cell they are staining, a well-established prostate basal cell marker that is a nuclear protein. Our results suggest ITIH5 serves as a novel basal cell marker for prostate tissue differential diagnosis on its own or in combination with other established markers. Biological role and significance of ITIH5 expression in prostate basal cells need to be elucidated.

items.title: TR-107 and Capivasertib Synergistically Inhibit Pancreatic Cancer Organoid Growth In Vitro
items.corresponding_institution: Stony Brook University Health Sciences Center School of Medicine: Stony Brook University Renaissance School of Medicine
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality in the United States, highlighting the need for effective therapeutic strategies. Oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) has emerged as a promising therapeutic target due to metabolic reprogramming and the pro-survival role of mitochondria in PDAC. The mitochondrial ClpXP complex, composed of the AAA+ ATPase ClpX and the peptidase ClpP, regulates mitochondrial homeostasis through protein degradation. Madera Therapeutics has developed novel ClpP activators, including TR-107. Here, we demonstrate that TR-107 reduces viability in four PDAC organoids and four cell lines at low-nanomolar concentrations while decreasing ClpX expression in a dose-dependent manner. Transcriptomic analysis revealed alterations in ferroptosis, amino acid metabolism, and HIF-1 signaling pathways. Notably, TR-107 retained its efficacy and mechanism of action under hypoxic conditions. Furthermore, TR-107 synergized with the AKT inhibitor capivasertib to suppress cell viability and modulate downstream signaling pathways. Collectively, these findings identify TR-107 as a promising therapeutic candidate that targets the mitochondrial ClpXP complex, disrupts mitochondrial function, and induces cellular stress and metabolic dysregulation. These effects may provide opportunities for combination therapies to improve treatment outcomes in PDAC.

items.title: Quasistable multiclonal carcinomas evolve through mutations with locally extended phenotypes
items.abstract: The earliest stages of epithelial carcinogenesis are often considered to arise via lineal evolution, a mutation-driven process characterised by purely competitive clonal interactions. However, this conventional view cannot fully explain the persistent polyclonality observed in many cancers. We therefore investigated an alternative mechanism of cancer progression, termed interclonal cooperation, arising from mutations that cause cells to produce microenvironmental changes, enabling them to affect the behaviours of surrounding cells. We built a Voronoi cell-based model (VCBM) of epithelial carcinogenesis evolution to examine the role of cancer cell interactions in proliferation, motility and degradation of the extracellular matrix (ECM) during the earliest stages of carcinogenesis. In this model, we considered mutations with four distinct effects on cells: impaired apoptosis, faster cell-cycling, hyperproliferation and enhanced invasiveness. In each case, these phenotypes can be either cell-autonomous, affecting only the mutated cell itself, or microenvironmental, affecting both the mutated cell and the surrounding cells within a specified range. Using our model, we investigated how microenvironmentally extended phenotypes in epithelial cells influence the formation of carcinogenic lesions. We found that the acquisition of microenvironmentally extended phenotypes reduces the overall mutational burden of the tissue by increasing the competitiveness of non-mutant cells with cells harbouring cell-autonomous mutations. However, progression from pre-malignancy to malignancy can occur without the acquisition of additional mutations, through field collision, i.e. by the growth and/or migration of mutually beneficial clones, leading to their co-localisation, which enables malignant interactions. Our results also indicate that mutations with microenvironmentally extended phenotypes can enhance the speed with which malignancy occurs compared with cell-autonomous phenotypes, through symbiotic clonal interactions. An important contribution to the speed of carcinogenesis is the ability of microenvironmentally extended phenotypes to overcome mutual inhibition of pro-malignant intracellular signalling pathways. Moreover, we found that, after an initial period of rapid change and clonal succession during carcinogenesis, genetically distinct clones of cell types persist together for long periods, maintaining stable proportions.

items.title: Targeting Telomere Integrity Enhances Radiosensitivity and Reveals Adaptive DNA Damage Response Vulnerabilities in Diffuse Midline Glioma
items.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG), including diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG), remains one of the most lethal pediatric malignancies, with limited durable benefit from radiotherapy (RT) due in part to adaptive DNA damage response (DDR) mechanisms. Here, we investigated whether targeting telomere integrity with the telomerase substrate analogue 6-thio-2'-deoxyguanosine (6-thio-dG; THIO) could induce therapeutically exploitable DNA damage in patient-derived DIPG models. THIO selectively suppressed DIPG cell proliferation while sparing telomerase-negative normal diploid fibroblasts and induced telomere dysfunction, as evidenced by increased telomere dysfunction-induced foci (TIFs), {gamma}H2AX accumulation, G2/M checkpoint arrest, and apoptosis. In orthotopic DIPG xenografts, THIO increased intratumoral TIF formation, suppressed tumor growth, and prolonged survival. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed activation of cellular stress-response pathways and downregulation of E2F genes, mitotic, and metabolism-associated gene programs. Mechanistically, THIO-induced progressive genomic and telomeric damage was associated with sequential activation of ATM and ATR signaling, consistent with engagement of adaptive DDR pathways. Combining THIO with ionizing radiation (IR) produced synergistic antitumor effects across three independent DIPG models representing distinct H3 mutation subtypes, with increased G2/M accumulation, genomic and telomeric DNA damage, and apoptotic cell death. In vivo, THIO combined with IR significantly improved therapeutic efficacy and prolonged median survival compared with monotherapy, including RT alone. Notably, pharmacologic inhibition of ATM or ATR attenuated THIO-induced checkpoint arrest and increased apoptosis, implicating DDR checkpoint signaling as an adaptive survival dependency following telomere damage. Collectively, these findings identify telomere-directed DNA damage as a promising therapeutic approach for DMG and provide a mechanistic rationale for combining THIO with RT and DDR checkpoint inhibition.

items.title: Exponent Polytopes for Abstracting Chemical Reaction Networks into Formal Specification Models for Compositional Design of Biomolecular Circuits
items.abstract: Model based design has shown promise for synthetic biological circuits. However, many approaches remain empirical and limited in scale. Here, we develop specification models from chemical reaction network (CRN) models. These specifications encode assumptions explicitly and guarantees that must be met under those assumptions. Specifically, we show how monomial dominance relations in open CRNs induce polyhedral regime assumptions in logarithmic coordinates. These assumptions give polyhedral assume guarantee contracts that encode system behavior. Further, we show how order of magnitude dominance assumptions can be written explicitly as contract assumptions and used to derive tighter guarantees. We demonstrate two biological circuit design applications: identifying the biological mechanisms that meet the required system-level specification, and screening promoter and ribosome binding site choices to determine expression gains that satisfy a specification through contract composition and refinement. Ultimately, these results provide a path from CRN descriptions of synthetic biological parts to specification-based compositional design.

items.title: CDK phospho-degron tags for dynamic protein regulation
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Bioengineering, University of Tartu
items.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) activity underpins cell cycle progression through dynamic and temporally ordered phosphorylation events. While transcriptional regulation has been extensively exploited in synthetic biology, the rational engineering of post-translational signaling circuits remains underdeveloped. Here, we introduce modular CDK-responsive phospho-degron tags derived from the Far1 regulatory region and demonstrate their ability to confer tunable, cell cycle-dependent control over protein stability in budding yeast. By systematically modifying cyclin docking motifs and Cks1 priming sites, we generate degron variants with distinct degradation kinetics and phosphorylation thresholds. These modules enable predictable modulation of transcription factor abundance and downstream gene expression. We further combine CDK-responsive degrons with phosphorylation-controlled localization modules for multi-layered regulation of sequential nuclear import and degradation. We encode multiple kinase activity thresholds within a single protein, demonstrating how complex phosphorylation logic can be compactly implemented. Finally, we show that degron performance is strongly influenced by culture conditions, particularly cell density and associated changes in CDK activity. Together, our results establish CDK-driven phospho-degrons as versatile building blocks for engineering dynamic protein regulation and provide a foundation for constructing synthetic post-translational signaling circuits.

items.title: Beyond the rule of seven: translating time across humans and dogs shows diverse clocks set the pace of development and aging
items.abstract: Although a dog's year is often converted to human age by multiplying it by seven, there is little scientific evidence to justify this calculation. Here, we assembled 11,365 observations to generate age alignments across multiple organ systems from humans and 11 canid species and 171 dog groups. We used a range of metrics, including behavioral milestones (e.g., age of eye opening), age-related changes in blood chemistry profiles, disease occurrence, and reproductive traits to translate ages across species and breeds. Our analyses revealed that the pace of development and aging varies across life stages and systems. For example, we found that dogs progress through postnatal development relatively more rapidly than humans. We also found that many biological processes vary relatively independently of each other across and within canid species. Models incorporating system-specific heterochronies across dog breeds outperformed models that assumed breeds differ only in their overall rates of development and aging. These findings demonstrate that estimating a dog's human-equivalent age by a factor, or a handful of traits, oversimplifies a complex pattern in rates of development and aging. Instead, the pace of aging is dictated from diverse biological clocks.

items.title: The Ran-binding protein Mog1 sustains Spt5 C-terminal phosphorylation by counteracting Spt4 in budding yeast
items.corresponding_institution: Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Cientificas IBV
items.abstract: Transcription elongation by RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) requires phosphorylation of the C-terminal repeat (CTR) of the elongation factor Spt5 by the Bur1-Bur2 kinase, yet how this modification is sustained remains unclear. Here we identify the conserved Ran cofactor Mog1 as a positive determinant of Spt5 CTR phosphorylation in budding yeast. Cells lacking Mog1 show reduced Spt5 phosphorylation and chromatin association, lower RNAPII CTD Ser2 phosphorylation and a previously unreported, guanine-reversible sensitivity to nucleotide depletion. These defects are mediated by Spt4, which accumulates in mog1{Delta} cells without a change in its nucleoplasmic distribution, and deleting SPT4 restores Spt5 phosphorylation, H2B monoubiquitination and H3K4 trimethylation, and normal growth and morphology. Both Spt4-Spt5 subunits, but neither BUR kinase subunit, co-purify with Mog1. Deleting the demethylase JHD2 restores H3K4me3 without rescuing growth, establishing the chromatin defects as consequences, not causes, of the elongation defect. Bur1 abundance and activation are unaffected in mog1{Delta} cells, and reducing BUR activity partially compensates rather than aggravates the loss of Mog1, indicating that Mog1 acts on the Spt4-Spt5 substrate; synthetic sickness with ctk1{Delta} places its contribution in early elongation. We propose that Spt4 imposes a limit on Spt5 CTR phosphorylation and that Mog1 counteracts this constraint.

items.title: An extended Cks1-interacting region in Far1 modulates Cdk1 inhibition and substrate phosphorylation
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Bioengineering, University of Tartu
items.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) use multiple docking interactions to recognise their substrates and inhibitors, but how sequences between canonical interaction motifs contribute to these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we identify an auxiliary interaction element in the budding yeast CDK inhibitor Far1 and investigate its contribution to kinase inhibition and multisite phosphorylation. Combining AlphaFold3 modelling with biochemical assays and mutational analysis, we show that Far1 residues 310-319 (QLIRTADISC), located immediately downstream of the Cks1-binding phospho-threonine T306, contribute to inhibition of Clb5-Cdk1. In particular, the hydrophobic residues I312 and I317 are important for inhibitory potency, consistent with their predicted positions at the Cks1-Cdk1 interface. To investigate the functional consequences of this interaction in a substrate context, we introduced the Far1 sequence between two phosphorylation sites in a Sic1-derived substrate. This insertion increased the accumulation of doubly phosphorylated product by more than twofold, while reducing the overall phosphorylation rate. These findings suggest that sequences between canonical CDK recognition elements can provide auxiliary interactions that influence both kinase inhibition and substrate phosphorylation dynamics. Thus, the region between established docking motifs represents an additional determinant of CDK substrate processing and inhibitory activity.

items.title: Age-dependent phosphorylation of estrogen receptor beta (ERβ) regulates homodimer formation and impairs the repression of amyloid precursor protein (APP) promoter.
items.corresponding_institution: Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine
items.abstract: Estrogen receptor beta (ER{beta}) is a ligand-activated nuclear steroid receptor that promotes neuroprotection through its transcriptional coordination of healthy cell gene programs. However, circulating estrogens are dramatically reduced post-menopause and the administration of hormone replacement therapy is only beneficial within a narrowly restricted timeframe after the menopause transition. The molecular underpinnings for this failure of ER{beta} to evoke protection in advanced age is unknown. Evidence suggests that age-related changes in protein-protein interactions could preclude ER{beta} genomic signaling. Protein-protein interactions can be regulated and modified through post-translational modifications (PTM)s of individual amino acid residues; the most well-studied PTM being phosphorylation. Our prior work showed that ER{beta} phosphorylation was age-dependent leading to the hypothesis that ER{beta} phosphorylation is required for ER{beta}-protein interactions, specifically ER{beta} homodimer formation. We used fluorescence lifetime measurements to quantify Forster resonance energy transfer (FRET) of ER{beta}-S176, S200, and Y488 phosphomutant protein interactions. Overall, our results demonstrate that phosphorylation of ER{beta}-S176, S200, and Y488 reduced ER{beta} homodimer formation, suggesting an age-dependent molecular mechanism that regulates ER{beta} genomic signaling. Moreover, phosphorylation at S200 and Y488 resulted in a loss of ER{beta}-mediated amyloid precursor protein (APP) promoter gene repression providing evidence that these age-dependent PTMs directly impact ER{beta}'s function as a transcription factor. Taken together, these data suggest that age-dependent changes in ER{beta} phosphorylation result in decreased ER{beta} genomic signaling, which could reduce the neuroprotective effects of estrogens following menopause.

items.title: LIFE-seq: longitudinal spatial transcriptomics of living tissue
items.corresponding_institution: State Key Laboratory of Digital Medical Engineering, School of Biological Science & Medical Engineering, Southeast University, Nanjing 210096, China
items.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has deepened our understanding of cellular spatial heterogeneity, yet existing technologies are predominantly confined to fixed or frozen specimens, limiting longitudinal molecular profiling of the same living tissue. To overcome this limitation, we developed LIFE-seq (Living-tissue in situ nanoforest extraction for spatiotemporal transcriptomic mapping), a minimally invasive approach that combines high-density nanoforest arrays for molecular sampling with directed transfer onto spatially barcoded messenger RNA (mRNA) capture chips. LIFE-seq enables spatial transcriptomic profiling while preserving overall tissue integrity and provides a modular strategy with the potential to integrate different 3'-end capture platforms. Performance validation demonstrated high concordance in global transcriptomic profiles and spatial gene expression patterns between nanoforest-derived replicas and conventional tissue sections, as well as faithful recapitulation of pathological features in a traumatic brain injury (TBI) model. Furthermore, longitudinal spatial transcriptomic profiling of cortical injury in the same mouse revealed temporally distinct injury responses, progressive activation of immune-associated gene programs, and spatially heterogeneous cell-type-specific expression changes. By enabling repeated molecular sampling and spatial transcriptomic analysis of living tissue, LIFE-seq provides a versatile framework for investigating tissue dynamics and pathological progression in vivo.

items.title: LAMP sheds light on how sequence to function models learn variant effects during post-training
items.abstract: Genomic sequence-to-function (S2F) models show promise for interpreting noncoding genetic variation, yet they currently underestimate the effects of most causal variants. This leads to fine-mapping failures that are reflected in their underperformance relative to linear baselines at predicting gene expression across individuals from personal genome sequences. Improving personal genome predictions, which reflect this underestimation, is therefore critical. There is broad interest in post-training S2F models to improve these predictions, yet many groups have shown that doing so with personal genome sequences and paired expression values does not meaningfully improve predictions on held-out genes and people (HOGP). Why these post-training efforts to improve predictions on HOGP, and therefore causal variant underestimation, remains unclear. To understand why, we introduce LAMP (Learning of Artificial Motif Perturbations), a framework in which artificial SNVs (aSNVs) perturbing transcription factor motifs are substituted into personal genome datasets genome-wide with large, consistent, and causal effects on gene expression. These aSNVs are designed to be deliberately easy to learn, yet fine-tuning Enformer using this LAMP framework led to persistent underperformance on HOGP, which suggests fundamental challenges for learning variant effects during post-training that are independent of the complexity of natural genetic variation. Our findings suggest this underperformance is caused in part due to challenges learning to strengthen enhancer-gene links during post-training. In particular, models struggle with learning to rewire attention weights to relate aSNV detection, over distance, to a change in expression of the target gene. This limitation is caused by strong pre-trained priors that downweight distal regulatory elements, causing extreme data inefficiency in learning to attend to distal elements, and variants within them, during post-training. Second, sequence variability between loci containing different instances of the same TF motif obscures otherwise easy-to-learn motif perturbation patterns and also hinder learning of variant effects. Our results suggest that the scale of observed human genetic variation is vastly insufficient to maximize S2F model accuracy on HOGP via simple fine-tuning, consistent with past outcomes. We propose data augmentation strategies that, under LAMP, significantly improve learning of aSNV effects by strategically targeting the limitations we identified. We release LAMP as a tool to troubleshoot and optimize future S2F post-training objectives.

items.title: Mathematical genomics of hidden signatures in NCF1: implications for chronic granulomatous disease
items.abstract: Inborn errors of immunity (IEIs), such as Chronic Granulomatous Disease (CGD), impose a disproportionately severe clinical burden in populations with high rates of consanguinity. CGD is caused by defects in the phagocyte NADPH oxidase complex, frequently due to mutations in the NCF1 gene encoding the p47phox protein. While the functional domains of NCF1 are well characterized, the quantitative architectural constraints governing its structural stability remain elusive. This study aimed to decipher the multidimensional quantitative signatures of NCF1, across diverse organisms in order to understand its conserved spatial sequence architecture and the structural basis of variant severity. We analyzed 41 NCF1 sequences using ten distinct quantitative features, integrating primary sequence metrics, biophysical chemistry, and abstract topological geometry. The synthesis of these features revealed a lack of a unified proximity matrix, demonstrating that NCF1 is defined by feature-dependent, multidimensional individual signatures. Primary sequence metrics exhibited rigid phylogenetic conservation, revealing invariant zero-entropy blocks that correlated strictly with severe CGD-causing mutations, while topological metrics exposed a deep spatial architectural convergence. These multidimensional baselines confirmed that the protein requires a highly specific spatial packing to assemble the NADPH oxidase complex; pathogenic mutations therefore disrupt precise structural signatures rather than globally destroying the protein. Consistent with this, the AlphaFold model places the folded PX and tandem SH3 domains in a high-confidence core and the regulatory C-terminal tail in an exposed, low-confidence region, supporting a tail-mediated autoinhibitory mechanism. Ultimately, this quantitative framework offers a useful perspective on NCF1 architecture and may serve as a supportive tool for evaluating the severity of clinical variants, contributing to precision medicine efforts for NCF1-associated diseases.

items.title: Optimal combined chemotherapeutic and antibiotic treatment for cancer in the presence of saboteur bacteria
items.corresponding_institution: Hungarian Centre of Excellence for Molecular Medicine
items.abstract: We consider a mathematical model of cancer dynamics under chemotherapeutic treatment in the presence of bacteria capable of metabolizing the chemotherapeutic agent, thereby compromising therapeutic efficacy. To counteract this effect, we investigate the introduction of antibiotic co-therapy aimed at eradicating the bacterial population or at least mitigating its negative impact on treatment outcomes. The underlying dynamics are formulated as a system of four non-linear ordinary differential equations, with the time-varying dosages of both drugs treated as control variables. Applying optimal control theory, we explore which combined treatment strategy leads to the best outcome, and how it is influenced by the model parameters. Convergence to the optimal control is achieved by employing a relaxation method within the forward-backward sweep algorithm. Furthermore, we analyze a discrete-dose variant of the optimal control problem, providing a more clinically realistic framework for scheduled drug administration.

items.title: A Latent Variable Perspective on EEG Measures of Attentional Control
items.abstract: Attentional control is a core cognitive function, yet there is still a significant debate revolving around its definition, factorial structure and underlying neural mechanisms. Research in this domain has largely developed along two largely disconnected traditions. Psychometric approaches assess individual differences using latent-variable models (e.g., structural equation modeling, confirmatory factor analysis), while cognitive neuroscience focuses on group-level behavioral and neural effects. This raises a critical question: can neural measures robust at the group level validly capture stable individual differences? Or more specifically, can some of the principles and analytical methods adopted in individual-differences research be directly applied to neural correlates of attentional control? The current study aims to address this question. Electroencephalogram data were recorded from participants as they completed four attentional control paradigms: a change detection task, the go/no-go task, the Simon task, and the Stroop task. From each task, we extracted the P3 component and a data-driven decoding accuracy measure as indices of conflict processing and tested whether these neural measures load onto a common latent factor of attentional control. Results revealed weak and largely non-significant correlations. Structural-equation modeling provided no evidence for a common latent factor, despite robust within-task effects at the group level reflected both in the behavioral and the EEG parameters. These findings suggest that EEG components may lack the construct validity needed to reliably capture individual differences in attentional control.

items.title: In vitro and in vivo validation of recombinant Syrian hamster interferon-α
items.corresponding_institution: KU Leuven Department of Microbiology, Immunology and Transplantation, Rega Institute; Virology, Antiviral Drug and Vaccine Research Group, Laboratory of Molecul
items.abstract: The Syrian hamster (Mesocricetus auratus) is an important model for the study of viral pathogenesis and the development of antiviral drugs and vaccines, yet species-specific reagents remain scarce. Here, we validate the potent and specific activity of recombinantly expressed Syrian hamster maIFN-12-like protein (maIFN) in vitro and in vivo. MaIFN expressed in E. coli induced MX2 and ISG15 expression in both BHK21 hamster kidney cells as well as in primary hamster fibroblasts in a dose-dependent manner and EC50 values in low pg/mL range. Activation was strictly STAT2-dependent and more potent, by at least one order of magnitude, than that achieved by heterologous human or mouse IFN. ISG induction translated into a strong antiviral activity against YF17D virus replication in BHK21 cells as well as ISRE-dependent reporter expression in a newly established hamster reporter cell line. When tested in wild-type but not in STAT2-deficient hamsters, maIFN showed a physiologic, vigorous yet rapidly contracting systemic ISG response. Together these findings establish maIFN as a functional antiviral cytokine and valuable reagent for preclinical infectious disease research using Syrian hamsters.

items.title: An Optimized ChIP-sequencing protocol for transcription factors in embryonic mouse brains
items.abstract: Chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (ChIP-Seq) is widely used to identify genome-wide protein-chromatin interactions. However, obtaining reliable ChIP-seq data for transcription factors has been challenging for several reasons, including their low abundance, transient or weak DNA binding, and poor antibody performance. Here, we present an improved ChIP-Seq protocol for mapping transcription factor occupancy in embryonic mouse brains. We describe critical steps in tissue preparation, fixation and antigen unmasking steps, and chromatin fragmentation by prolonged sonication, specifically optimized for transcription factors. Our key innovation is the application of antigen retrieval to freshly fixed tissues, a technique commonly used in immunohistochemistry to unmask epitopes masked by fixation, in combination with slow fixation and extensive sonication to enhance ChIP-seq performance. This approach enhances epitope accessibility and expands the range of antibodies suitable for ChIP-seq, providing a robust strategy for mapping the genome-wide occupancy of transcription factors that are otherwise challenging to study using conventional ChIP-seq methods.

items.title: Diffusion geometry and topology reveal Alzheimer's proteomic states
items.abstract: ABSTRACT INTRODUCTION: Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity. Identifying biologically distinct proteomic states may improve understanding of disease heterogeneity and support precision diagnostics. METHODS: Cerebrospinal fluid proteomic data from ADNI were analyzed. Among 6,361proteins tested between cognitively normal and AD groups, 407 remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (FDR < 0.05), with 404 retained after missingness filtering. Following preprocessing and outlier removal, 130 individuals were included. Diffusion geometry and persistent homology were applied to characterize intrinsic proteomic structure without predefined clusters. The framework was further evaluated in an independent mass spectrometry cohort. RESULTS: Persistent homology revealed multiscale organization of the AD proteomic landscape. At the selected H0 filtration scale, two dominant proteomic states (n = 71 and n = 42) contained most individuals, alongside smaller components. H1 persistence identified nontrivial cyclic structure, indicating continuous higher-order organization beyond discrete state partitions. The dominant states exhibited distinct proteomic profiles and differed substantially in tau-related biomarkers. Elevated tau pathology in one state was reproduced in the independent cohort, whereas A{beta}42 differences were less consistent across cohorts. DISCUSSION: AD proteomic heterogeneity is characterized by multiscale organization combining dominant group structure with continuous higher-order relationships.

items.title: Characterization of heterogeneous bioinformatics training needs in the AI era
items.abstract: Bioinformatics training providers serve heterogeneous audiences, and generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly changing what learners need. Training-needs surveys are typically analyzed question by question or split by demographics such as career stage. This assumes that people in the same demographic group need the same training, whereas needs may depend more on the data people work with. We present a protocol that groups survey respondents by the similarity of their topic ratings rather than by demographics. Respondents form a correlation network, and community detection identifies learner profiles with shared needs. Applied to the 2026 SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics training-needs survey (n=260), it yielded four profiles that were stable under resampling: AI and data, infectious disease genomics, functional genomics, and biochemistry, imaging & AI, each with distinct preferences and barriers. For example, the topic "LLM-based knowledge extraction" ranked 2nd overall but 16th for the infectious disease genomics profile, where "phylogenetics data analysis" (17th overall) ranked first. Across all profiles, respondents wanted training on AI and reproducible data practices but liked AI-assisted learning least of all formats. The protocol requires only Likert-type items on a shared scale, so other providers can reuse it to shape their training curricula.

items.title: Loss of metabolic resilience underlies maladaptive responses to lipid overload in TDP-43 proteinopathy
items.corresponding_institution: Neurological disorders group, Hospital Clinico San Carlos, IdISSC, Madrid, Spain
items.abstract: INTRODUCTION Altered eating behaviour is a hallmark feature of behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). These changes may represent a compensatory response to an underlying metabolic disturbance. However, whether increased lipid availability restores metabolic homeostasis or instead accelerates disease progression remains unknown. TDP-43 proteinopathies, which account for approximately half of FTD cases, are associated with alterations in lipid metabolism, providing a mechanistic framework to investigate the cerebral response to lipid overload. METHODS We combined clinical observations in patients with bvFTD with mechanistic studies in the physiological TardbpM323K/M323K knock-in mouse model to determine how TDP-43 dysfunction modifies the response to chronic lipid excess. RESULTS In the bvFTD cohort, elevated cholesterol and triglycerides were associated with poorer cognitive performance, while mutant mice fed a lifelong high-fat diet showed worse cognitive impairment. Multi-omics analyses of the frontal cortex revealed maladaptive metabolic rewiring characterized by impaired mitochondrial and cholesterol metabolism, lipid accumulation, and widespread remodelling of TDP-43-dependent RNA processing. These alterations affected synaptic function and neuronal communication and were accompanied by reduced cerebral glucose utilization measured by 18F-FDG PET, neurotransmitter imbalance and enhanced neuroinflammation. DISCUSSION Increased lipid availability fails to compensate for TDP-43-associated metabolic dysfunction and instead promotes maladaptive molecular and functional responses. These findings identify impaired metabolic resilience as feature of TDP-43-mediated neurodegeneration and suggest that altered eating behaviour in bvFTD may represent an unsuccessful attempt to counteract an underlying metabolic deficit rather than a purely behavioural symptom. Thus, the biological context may determine whether increased energy intake is beneficial or detrimental during neurodegeneration.

items.title: Correlated but distinct: VIP and NDNF interneurons implement dissociable inhibitory motifs for state-dependent gain control in visual cortex
items.abstract: VIP and NDNF positive interneurons are both found in layers 1 and 2/3 of the cortex, but have distinct patterns of gene expression, morphology, and connectivity. Despite this, their functional roles in the sensory cortices seem remarkably similar; their activity correlates with behavioral state, and they gate behaviorally driven increases in excitatory activity and sensory-driven responses. We sought to directly compare VIP and NDNF positive interneurons in the mouse visual cortex to determine if their activity was indeed functionally redundant or could be distinguished by their correlation to behavioral state, to excitatory activity, or to excitatory visual responses. Using simultaneous recordings of pupil diameter and running speed together with dual-population calcium imaging, we found that although the activity of both VIP and NDNF positive interneurons was more strongly correlated with behavior than was excitatory neuron activity, VIP positive interneuron activity was more strongly correlated with pupil diameter, whereas layer 2/3 NDNF positive interneuron activity was more strongly correlated with running speed. Excitatory-to-VIP pairwise correlation increased during locomotion, whereas excitatory-to-NDNF pairwise correlation decreased during locomotion. Intriguingly, although VIP-to-NDNF pairwise correlation was high, cortical depth significantly affected both VIP-to-NDNF correlation and the correlation of NDNF positive interneurons with pupil diameter and running speed. As expected, excitatory visual responses were significantly modulated by both pupil dilation and locomotion. However, we found that the level of VIP and NDNF activity preceding stimulus onset had a unique contribution to and was positively correlated with the amplitude of excitatory visual responses. Thus, while highly correlated to one another and to behavioral state, VIP and NDNF positive interneurons are functionally distinguishable in their relationship to both behavior and excitatory activity in the mouse visual cortex.

items.title: Drug Repurposing of Rapamycin Mitigates Amyloid-β-Associated Proteotoxicity in Caenorhabditis elegans Models of Alzheimer's Disease
items.abstract: Background: Alzheimers disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia worldwide, affecting an estimated 55 million people and projected to exceed 130 million by 2050. AD is defined pathologically by extracellular accumulation of amyloid-beta (A{beta}) and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles. Currently no therapy halts the underlying neurodegeneration in AD patients. Proteotoxic accumulation of A{beta} is a central pathogenic event therefore, strategies that enhance its clearance represent a compelling therapeutic avenue. Rapamycin (sirolimus), an FDA-approved allosteric inhibitor of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) that relieves mTORC1-mediated suppression of autophagy, positioning it as an attractive drug-repurposing candidate for AD. However, it remains unclear whether rapamycins neuroprotection depends on directly reducing A{beta} burden or acts through A{beta}-independent mechanisms. This question, along with whether rapamycin alters specific A{beta} species, has not been systematically examined in a single, genetically tractable model. Methods/Results: Using two transgenic C. elegans models of human A{beta} expression a temperature-inducible, muscle-specific strain CL4176 and the pan-neuronal strain CL2355. We exposed C. elegans to 20 M rapamycin the lowest, nontoxic concentration to produce a protective effect. Rapamycin treatment delayed A{beta} induced paralysis in log-rank p = 0.0001) and improved crawling and swimming locomotion parameters. In the pan-neuronal CL2355 strain, rapamycin rescued the A{beta} induced chemotaxis deficit (one-way ANOVA, p = 0.008) without altering chemotaxis in the non-transgenic CL2122 control. Rapamycin also extended Kaplan Meier survival in CL2355 and preserved locomotor health span, delaying the trajectory of age related motor decline. At the molecular level, rapamycin did not significantly affect A{beta} burden. Conclusion: Rapamycin provides broad-spectrum and A{beta}-selective neuroprotection across muscle and neuron expressing C. elegans models of A{beta} proteotoxicity, extending from paralysis and locomotion to chemosensory behavior, longevity, and health span.

items.title: Slow but not fast theta tACS modulation of hippocampal-cortical connectivity compresses temporal distance judgments
items.abstract: The temporal organization of episodic memory is thought to depend critically on the hippocampus, potentially coordinated by theta-band oscillations. Here, we used concurrent transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to examine whether slow theta stimulation (3 Hz) applied over the left parietal cortex modulates hippocampal-cortical functional connectivity during memory encoding, and how this relates to subsequent temporal memory performance. Twenty-seven participants encoded sequences of object-scene pairs that were presented either within a single context or across a context boundary, under different tACS conditions (3 Hz, 8 Hz, and no stimulation), and afterwards judged the temporal distance between item pairs. Behaviorally, 3 Hz stimulation led to significantly compressed temporal distance judgments compared to 8 Hz, suggesting altered temporal memory reconstruction. Further, 3 Hz tACS selectively reduced hippocampal connectivity with occipital cortex, comprising left calcarine and lateral occipital clusters, and reduced hippocampal activity during encoding. In contrast, 8 Hz tACS reduced connectivity between the stimulation site and right early visual cortex. Neither frequency modulated hippocampal-cortical connectivity during retrieval. These results suggest that slow theta oscillations can shape hippocampal-cortical network dynamics in a frequency-specific manner, influencing the construction of temporal relations in memory.

items.title: Subtractive and Divisive Methods for Isolating Neural Oscillations From Broadband Activity Yield Different, Even Conflicting, Power Estimates
items.abstract: Understanding the role of oscillatory brain activity in cognition is a key objective in cognitive neuroscience. However, quantifying the power of narrowband neural oscillations is made challenging by the presence of non-oscillatory broadband activity in the signal. Recently, there has been a proliferation of methods designed to separate oscillatory from non-oscillatory (aperiodic) signals. To perform this separation, these methods must model the relationship between oscillatory and aperiodic components. Crucially, however, such methods rarely explicitly clarify whether they assume that this relationship is additive or multiplicative, an issue compounded by the common use of log-transformed data (i.e., subtraction in log space is equivalent to division in linear space). Here, we show the importance of justifying which assumption about component relations is applied. Using simulated power spectra with additive oscillatory and aperiodic components, we illustrate that methods that assume a multiplicative model, such as the popular specparam (formerly fooof) toolbox, systematically mis-estimate oscillatory activity in ways that can obscure real oscillatory differences between conditions, or even reverse their sign, creating an illusory effect. We then demonstrate these effects in two complementary empirical datasets: (a) a cross-sectional, between-subjects analysis of age-related differences in alpha power, showing how separation approaches impact effect size and detectability; and (b) a within-subjects analysis of pre-stimulus changes in alpha power in a detection task, showing how switching between approaches can greatly reduce the evidence for an effect, leading to different conclusions. These results highlight that researchers must explicitly report and justify assumptions about aperiodic and oscillatory signal combination, as these assumptions have implications not only for analyses of oscillatory activity and resultant conclusions, but also for integration of results across reports (which may implicitly employ different assumptions), and ultimately for the development of theories regarding electrophysiological features and their putative relations to cognition.

items.title: Differential modulation of host cell Serine and Arginine-Rich (SR) protein and apoptotic factor BCL-2 gene expressions during Chandipura and Dengue virus infections
items.corresponding_institution: Amity Institute of Biotechnology, Amity University, Noida
items.abstract: Regulation of alternative splicing (AS) is important in controlling cellular functions. More than 95% human genes are alternatively spliced and AS is regulated by close to 100 splicing factors. Line of evidences suggest that virus infections alter the AS pattern of numerous host genes. In this study we have investigated Chandipura virus (CHPV) induced alteration of host cell SR protein gene expressions and determined if these changes have any effect on apoptotic factor BCL-2 levels. CHPV is a negative stranded RNA virus which causes fever, brain encephalitis and death among young children with a case-fatality rate of 50%. Few studies were done in past to understand the roles of host factors in CHPV pathogenesis and no study was done on virus induced changes in AS. Our study showed that there is a down-regulation of SR proteins SRp55 and SRp75 expression levels significantly decreased in the CHPV infected Vero E6 cells compared to uninfected cells. For a comparison, we also looked at the levels of SRp55 and SRp75 in dengue virus (DENV) infected cells. Our results showed that SRp75 levels is unchanged whereas SRp55 levels increased in DENV infected cells. We have also determined the levels of large and small splice variants of apoptotic gene BCL-2 to find out possible correlation between the altered splicing factor expressions and virus infected cell death via apoptosis. Our data indicates that in CHPV infected cells, BCL-2 large splice variant expressions decreased as compared to uninfected cells. This is the first study of CHPV mediated alteration of splicing factor expressions and these results warrant further study with other viruses to better understand the global changes in host splicing events, cell survival, host immune response during virus infection.

items.title: Progerin Expression in Alveolar Epithelial Cells Exacerbates Inflammatory Responses to SARS-CoV-2 Infection
items.abstract: Age is a major determinant of severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), yet the cell-intrinsic consequences of ageing for SARS-CoV-2 infection remain difficult to examine in human experimental systems. Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived tissues provide accessible models of infection but generally lack hallmarks of ageing. Here, we employed an iPSC line containing an inducible progerin cassette and differentiated these cells towards an alveolar type II-like epithelial fate. Progerin induction in differentiated cells increased DNA-damage-associated {gamma}H2AX staining and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, reduced the heterochromatin-associated mark H3K9me3, and induced transcriptional programs associated with extracellular matrix remodeling, fibrosis and inflammation. Following infection with authentic SARS-CoV-2, progerin-expressing cultures exhibited a greater perturbation of the host transcriptome, including increased interferon-associated and inflammatory gene signatures. Transcriptomic analysis support higher viral RNA abundance in the aged model, and this was further confirmed by functional assays that showed increased infectious activity from condition media. Together, these data establish a temporally controlled model of selected ageing-associated phenotypes in human alveolar epithelial-like cells and suggest that progerin-induced cellular stress can amplify epithelial responses to SARS-CoV-2. More broadly, these findings distinguish epithelial-intrinsic inflammatory priming from the multicellular pathology of severe COVID-19.

items.title: Expanding the human T cell receptor germline reference through population-scale pangenome analysis using the gAIRR Suite version 2
items.abstract: The germline gene set encoding the adaptive immune receptor repertoire (gAIRR) defines the allele space from which the expressed repertoire (exprAIRR) is assembled, so an incomplete gAIRR reference propagates errors into T cell receptor (TR) annotation and genotyping and is also a barrier to studying inherited TR variation in its own right. Human TR gAIRR diversity remains incompletely characterized because the loci resist short-read resolution and because locus-resolved cohorts have been small. We developed gAIRR Suite version 2, in which each gAIRR-annotate query carries 50 bp of germline sequence on either side of the allele core and a call is reported only when the assembly supports the core together with both flanks, and in which gAIRR-call genotypes from Element AVITI libraries whose 500-bp Read 1 spans a complete V core with its flanking anchors. Applying this framework to Human Pangenome Reference Consortium Release 2 (464 haplotype-resolved assemblies from 232 individuals across five superpopulations), we identified 531 novel TR alleles (486 TRV, 45 TRJ), each observed in the targeted-sequencing reads of at least one carrier, of which 298 were absent from our 47-individual Release 1 catalogue. In 216 individuals, targeted genotyping with gAIRR-seq and gAIRR-call recovered 99.985% of the 61,628 evaluated alleles found in the corresponding assemblies, with a precision of 99.995%. Release 2 added few common alleles but many rare ones: 407 of the 531 were restricted to a single superpopulation, and African-ancestry individuals accounted for 51.1% of these (46.0% {+/-} 2.1% after downsampling to equal group size) while comprising 30.2% of the cohort. Population-scale pangenome analysis therefore extends the TR gAIRR reference chiefly by recovering variation that smaller or less diverse cohorts would miss.

items.title: GatorAnchor: Cross-Modal Uncertainty-Aware Learning of Reliable Cell Neighborhoods in Single-Cell Multi-Omics
items.abstract: Cross-modal uncertainty challenges single-cell multi-omics integration because molecular modalities differ in sparsity, technical noise, and context-dependent biological informativeness, producing discordant cell-cell relationships. Treating conflicting evidence as equally reliable can propagate uncertain relationships and obscure biologically meaningful cellular heterogeneity. GatorAnchor is a cross-modal uncertainty-aware framework that learns modality-specific probabilistic representations, quantifies disagreement across modalities and neighborhood evidence sources, and refines cell-cell relationships according to their reliability. Across ten paired transcriptome-protein and transcriptome-chromatin datasets, GatorAnchor achieves the highest mean performance across four evaluation metrics among nine representative integration methods, demonstrating improved resolution of cellular heterogeneity. Candidate relations with greater composite unreliability show lower consistency with reference cell-type structure, whereas filtering highly unreliable relations increases same-type edge purity across all datasets. Modality conflict is associated with transcript-protein measurement discordance, while transcriptome-chromatin analyses reveal lineage-dependent contributions of molecular and decoder-derived evidence. A three-modality transcriptome-chromatin-protein analysis characterizes cluster of differentiation 4 (CD4)-related communities with distinct molecular profiles and consistent within-donor contrasts across 12 donors. Under incomplete and mosaic measurements, GatorAnchor preserves informative cell-population structure, while cross-modal correspondence increasingly depends on paired-cell anchors. These findings support uncertainty-aware neighborhood refinement for reliable and interpretable characterization of cellular heterogeneity.

items.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Antibiotic Resistance Genes: Performance, Interpretability, and Cross-Database Redundancy
items.abstract: Antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) classifiers are typically developed and evaluated within a single curated database, leaving open how much two independently curated databases agree and what that implies for apparent cross-database generalization. We trained an XGBoost classifier on amino acid trigram frequencies and physicochemical descriptors using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD), the field's largest curated ARG resource. The model separated resistance genes from non-resistance proteins with near-ceiling accuracy (AUROC = 0.982, MCC = 0.886); a label-shuffling null baseline collapsed to chance (AUROC = 0.508) and bootstrap confidence intervals were narrow, confirming genuine signal rather than data leakage or overfitting. SHAP analysis attributed this performance to biologically interpretable features, notably the trigram KTG, isoelectric point, and aromaticity, each consistent with known catalytic motifs in resistance enzymes. Before testing the classifier against ResFinder, one of CARD's most widely used counterparts, we assessed database independence by clustering sequences with CD-HIT, finding that 96.8-98.7% of ResFinder sequences shared substantial protein identity with CARD even at a permissive 50% identity threshold, indicating the two databases largely represent the same sequence population, with direct implications for how cross-database generalization should be measured. On the small subset of ResFinder sequences genuinely non-redundant with CARD (40-100 sequences, depending on threshold), the classifier failed completely, never classifying any as resistance genes; SHAP traced this failure to sequence length, as non-redundant sequences are nearly three times longer than training proteins, and length is among the model's most influential features. The same pattern emerged by resistance mechanism: the model achieved perfect accuracy on beta-lactamases, compact single-domain enzymes well represented in training (100%, n = 351), but correctly identified only 38.5% of efflux pump components (n = 13), a mechanism built from large, multi-domain transporters rather than compact catalytic enzymes. Together, these results describe a capable, interpretable ARG classifier alongside a quantified methodological caution: cross-database redundancy must be measured rather than assumed, and when a sequence-composition classifier fails, the failure is often explained by protein architecture rather than database origin.

items.title: Infectious Disease Knowledge Graph (IDKG) for Antiviral and Antibacterial Drug Discovery.
items.abstract: Infectious diseases remain a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, while therapeutic discovery is hindered by fragmented biomedical data and antimicrobial resistance. To address this challenge, we developed the Infectious Disease Knowledge Graph (IDKG), a queryable platform that integrates curated chemical, biological, pharmacological, and clinical information relevant to infectious-disease drug discovery. Using a customized ORION pipeline, we integrated 20 data sources, including DrugCentral, SMACC, Heli-SMACC, NPASS, ClinicalTrials.gov, and host-virus interaction databases, into a Neo4j graph containing more than 4.6 million nodes and 26 million edges. IDKG supports graph-based reasoning through Clinical Outcome Pathways (COPs) and incorporates curation workflows for small molecules, biologics, and complex mixtures. Illustrative applications include reconstruction of a literature-supported remdesivir pathway for COVID-19 and graph-based mechanistic interpretation of experimentally observed quorum-sensing inhibitor-antibiotic synergies in multidrug-resistant bacteria. The platform provides an interoperable framework for drug repurposing, target prioritization, and mechanism-based hypothesis generation. IDKG is freely available at https://idkg.mml.unc.edu.

items.title: Attenuated, Not Absent. Trusting Autonomous Systems Tracks Reliability More Closely, With Less Neural Engagement, Than Trusting Humans
items.abstract: Users of autonomous systems and AI assistants decide whether to accept a system's output, yet whether such active trust decisions engage the same evaluative architecture as trust between people remains unknown. Forty-four participants made trial-by-trial decisions to trust or distrust a human or autonomous system partner during fMRI, with identical prescripted accuracy for both partners across five difficulty levels. Despite equivalent performance, trust in humans exceeded their reliability. At the highest difficulty level, the estimated probability of trusting the human partner was 72% but only 51% for the system, despite both performing at 52% accuracy. Distrust decisions recruited a prespecified performance monitoring network of valuation, salience, social-perceptual and affective regions. On hard trials, this network remained functionally coupled for both partners. Across the task, trust and distrust were discriminable in every component for both, with greater distrust-related activation and discriminability for human partners. Discriminability differences were expressed on hard trials, where partner accuracy was uncertain and trust diverged between partners. These findings indicate that trust in humans and autonomous systems engages a shared evaluative architecture, but that engagement is attenuated during autonomous system interaction. Whereas our earlier passive monitoring study found the P3a to system errors absent with no behavioural difference, an active decision appears to impose a floor of engagement, so that technology-related cognitive economization, a reduction in cognitive and social-affective resources for non-human partners, takes the form of attenuation rather than absence. Alongside this attenuation, trust in the system tracked its reliability without exceeding it.

items.title: A multiscale map of the descending sympathetic innervation of the spleen
items.corresponding_institution: Allen Institute, Brain Science, Neurobiology of Action and Neural Dynamics, Seattle, WA United States; Zuckerman Mind Brain Behavior Institute, Columbia Univers
items.abstract: Brain regulation of visceral organ function depends on descending neural circuits. The spleen is the largest secondary lymphoid organ, and studies indicate that descending neural activity can alter splenic immune responses. Here, we combined retrograde tracing, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spinal cord and brain reconstruction, and glycoprotein-complemented rabies tracing to map the sympathetic circuits associated with these organs in mice. Catecholaminergic fibers densely innervated the spleen and pancreas, and retrograde labeling identified largely distinct populations of postganglionic neurons within the celiac-superior mesenteric ganglion complex (CMG). Spleen-projecting neurons were enriched in suprarenal regions, whereas pancreas-projecting neurons were distributed more broadly. Single nucleus transcriptomics resolved three CMG neuron types and a Cre line marking the Rxfp1+ neurons labeled spleen-projecting neurons. CMG-projecting sympathetic preganglionic neurons occupied the intermediolateral cell column, intercalated nucleus, and spinal nucleus of the thoracic spinal cord. A tracing strategy designed to identify neurons upstream of these preganglionic populations labeled neurons in the medulla, pons, midbrain, hypothalamus, and several areas of the cortex including motor cortex. Motor-cortex axons formed vGlut1-positive boutons in close apposition to retrogradely labeled CMG-projecting neurons, providing anatomical support for a descending cortical route to sympathetic spinal circuits. These data provide an integrated anatomical and transcriptomic description of the descending circuits innervating the spleen and pancreas, and suggest that motor cortex is an effector cortex that controls more than movement through its projections to the spinal cord.

items.title: A neuronal atlas of neurexin isoform expression in Caenorhabditis elegans
items.abstract: The Caenorhabditis elegans neurexin gene nrx-1 encodes both long () and short ({gamma}) isoforms, but how their expression varies across individual neurons remains unclear. Using NeuroPAL and endogenous transcriptional reporters, we generated a nervous system-wide atlas of nrx-1 expression in L4 hermaphrodites. We assessed reporters for one and two {gamma} transcript groups in 267 identified neurons. The two {gamma} reporters collectively marked a broader set of neurons than the reporter, and most neurons expressing the reporter also expressed at least one {gamma} reporter. Among the ventral nerve cord motor neurons examined, reporter expression was restricted to cholinergic neurons, while one {gamma} reporter was detected exclusively in GABAergic neurons. The other {gamma} reporter was consistently detected in most cholinergic motor neurons and detected in only a subset of GABAergic motor neurons, often variably across animals. In two-fold embryos, this same {gamma} reporter was detected in more neurons than the reporter. Two upstream regulatory elements contributed to its expression in different neuronal populations. At dorsal nerve cord synapses, disruption of either isoform class reduced NRX-1 fluorescence, with a larger reduction after disruption of the short isoforms. By identifying neurons that express different combinations of long and short neurexins, this atlas provides a starting point for testing where the two isoform classes have distinct synaptic roles and where they may act together.

items.title: Near-threshold somatosensory perception revisited: Pre- and post-stimulus neural processes during electrical and naturalistic mechanical stimulation
items.corresponding_institution: Max Planck Institue for Human and Cognitive Brain Sciences
items.abstract: Near-threshold somatosensory stimulation is traditionally applied to investigate the post-stimulus neural correlates of conscious perception as well as ongoing brain activity like alpha oscillations that precede stimulation and modulate perception. Recent findings showed that applying more natural mechanical stimulation instead of the frequently used electric stimulation reveals differences in early post-stimulus perceptual correlates. The precise role of pre-stimulus alpha oscillations requires deeper investigation in the electrical modality and is yet fully undiscovered in the mechanical modality. In this study we investigate post-stimulus neural correlates of conscious perception and shine light on how pre-stimulus alpha amplitude and phase coherence relate to electrical and mechanical stimulus perception. Contrary to previous findings, we found no differences between modalities in early perceptual correlates. Both modalities showed robust correlates of stimulus perception likely corresponding to the N80 and N140 components. The effect of stimulus perception was localised in the right contralateral precentral and postcentral gyri, with the left ipsilateral hemisphere contributing shortly afterwards. We found a negative relationship between the pre-stimulus alpha oscillation amplitude and stimulus perception. Moreover, greater pre-stimulus alpha phase coherence coincided with an increase in stimulus perception. There was no evidence that the alpha effects differed between stimulation modalities.

items.title: In silico designed small molecule targets misfolded TDP-43 to rescue function and ALS pathology
items.abstract: The DNA/RNA binding protein TARDBP or TDP-43 is a key driver of pathology in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), a motor neuron disease with no known cure.
